title: Angels, Roll the Rock Away
description: Angels, Roll the Rock Away in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Gibbons wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 235 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ's Resurrection”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: An-gels, roll the rock a-way; Death, yield up thy might-y prey; See! he ris-es from the tomb, Glow-ing with im-mor-tal bloom.

lines: Angels, roll the rock away;
Death, yield up thy mighty prey;
See! he rises from the tomb,
Glowing with immortal bloom.
'T is the Saviour! Angels, raise
Fame's eternal trump of praise;
Let the earth's remotest bound
Hear the joy-inspiring sound.
Now, ye saints, lift up your eyes;
Now to glory see him rise
In long triumph up the sky —
Up to waiting worlds on high.
Praise him, all ye heavenly choirs,
Praise, and sweep your golden lyres;
Shout, O earth, in rapturous song;
Let the strains be sweet and strong.
Every note with wonder swell, —
And the Saviour's triumph tell;
Where, O death, is now thy sting?
Where thy terrors, vanquished king?

licence: Public domain: Thomas Gibbons died in 1785.
credits: Words by Thomas Gibbons (1720–1785), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
